  ],
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "Q1",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "What reporting window should the closed-ticket listing use: the previous calendar week, a rolling seven days, or another defined interval?",
      "changes": "The date filter, timezone, boundary tests, and documented API contract.",
      "route": "person",
      "default": "If no answer is available, record rolling seven days ending at query time in UTC, measured by closure time, with inclusive start and exclusive end.",
      "blocks": "The final window contract and its acceptance tests; discovery must first check the report, operational documentation, and any available support-lead reporting references. The repository's current weekly report counts all listed tickets and defines no time window."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q2",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "What counts as a sufficiently recent resolution notification, including pending or failed delivery?",
      "changes": "Suppression behavior and tests for sent, pending, dead, and boundary cases.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "Suppress a close notice for the same ticket when its resolution notice is pending or was sent within the preceding five minutes; a dead notice does not suppress it.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the default proceeds after discovery checks existing notification records and any documented policy."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q3",
      "category": "K1",
      "question": "How should immediate delivery and bulk anti-spam batching coexist?",
      "changes": "Notification grouping, timing, content, and delivery tests.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "Queue notifications immediately and use the existing worker cadence; combine eligible closures from the same bulk request by requester without exposing another requester's tickets. No cross-request waiting window is assumed.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the default proceeds after discovery establishes the existing outbox and notifier contracts and whether the worker can support grouping without changing retry logic."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q4",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "What bulk-close interface and per-ticket failure semantics should clients use?",
      "changes": "The request and response shape, validation, audit behavior, and 500-ticket boundary test.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "If discovery finds no existing contract, add one documented bulk-close HTTP operation accepting at least 500 ticket IDs, preserving lifecycle rules and reporting each result independently.",
      "blocks": "The bulk API contract until discovery checks routes, client conventions, body-size limits, persistence, and any available consumer references."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q5",
      "category": "K13",
      "question": "How do repeated closes satisfy both idempotency and the requested conflict response?",
      "changes": "Repeat-request status, side effects, audit entries, and tests.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "The first valid close changes state once; subsequent closes return 409 conflict without another state change, audit entry, or notification.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the default proceeds after discovery confirms the current transition and error contracts."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q6",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "What shared state, actor identity, visibility, and restart guarantees does the runtime already provide?",
      "changes": "Audit attribution, notification persistence, privacy expectations, and restart tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use X-Actor with the existing system fallback; preserve the existing optional single-owner data file and internal-network trust model. Assume no authenticated user identity, cross-process coordination, or per-user access control.",
      "blocks": "Any stronger identity, privacy, or concurrency guarantee until discovery checks the HTTP, storage, persistence, and deployment contracts."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q7",
      "category": "K2",
      "question": "Do all list filters combine as documented across pagination?",
      "changes": "The filter fix and HTTP-level regression tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Require every supplied filter to match before pagination.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: repository inspection already shows matchesFilters uses OR while the API documentation specifies AND; discovery should also check cursor behavior and other filter consumers."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q8",
      "category": "K6",
      "question": "Which runtime, configuration, dependencies, and seams must remain compatible?",
      "changes": "Implementation constraints and compatibility checks.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Keep Node.js 22 or later, built-in modules only, current environment settings, store-owned changes, existing outbox retry behavior, and the CLI raw-column contract.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: discovery confirms the configuration, persistence validation, and integration seams before implementation."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q9",
      "category": "K8",
      "question": "What evidence demonstrates the outcomes at their actual boundaries?",
      "changes": "Acceptance checks and the until-loop exit.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use npm test plus a running-server check covering close notification and suppression, bulk closure of 500 tickets, audit attribution, and combined closed-window filters; include meaningful boundary and failure cases.",
      "blocks": "A successful exit until discovery establishes the test harness, runtime access, and a way to observe delivery. This intake does not run tests or start a server."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q10",
      "category": "K9",
      "question": "Where must the completed change become usable and what access is available?",
      "changes": "Delivery and final verification.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Deliver the change in this ticket-service source checkout for its HTTP clients and notification consumers; no production release is assumed.",
      "blocks": "Release or deployed-target verification until discovery establishes an explicitly authorized target and access. Source changes in an isolated run become visible in the original checkout at final return; deployed behavior exists only after release."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q11",
      "category": "K12",
      "question": "Are the named until-loop and backchain workflows available in the execution host, and is there a relevant earlier run to resume?",
      "changes": "Workflow invocation, planning preconditions, and recovery.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the host's supplied descriptions: back-chain before implementation and continue until green tests and a running-server check pass. Treat Ralph-style overnight execution as optional and, if selected, cap it at 10 iterations or two hours, whichever comes first. No prior run is implied.",
      "blocks": "Starting the named workflows until discovery checks their installed instructions and any prior-run state; if unavailable, record that limitation rather than claim they ran."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q12",
      "category": "K11",
      "question": "Can grouping, suppression, and 500-ticket closure preserve atomic records and existing retry behavior?",
      "changes": "Design boundaries and early failure checks.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Preserve audit and outbox consistency, current retry and dead-letter semantics, and old saved-state compatibility; do not promise a numeric latency target.",
      "blocks": "A viable design until discovery checks persistence validation, transaction behavior, worker delivery, payload limits, and existing data. The 500-ticket call must work."
    }
  ],
  "summary": "S1 [fact]: Scope is the help-desk ticket service in this repository; the usable result belongs in its source checkout and service interfaces. S2 [fact; defaults Q2]: On closure, notify the requester in the established resolution-notification style while suppressing an overly recent duplicate. S3 [fact; default Q3]: Queue promptly and group eligible bulk closures by recipient without exposing other recipients' tickets. S4 [fact; open Q1]: Add a closed-ticket listing for the reporting window; the checked-in weekly report has no date window. S5 [fact]: Make all documented list filters conjunctive, including with pagination. S6 [fact]: Verify existing behavior; source inspection already identifies OR filtering contrary to the documented AND contract. S7 [fact; discovery Q9 and Q11]: Back-chain first and continue until tests pass and behavior works against a running server. S8 [fact; default Q11]: Overnight Ralph-style execution is optional and must be capped if chosen. S9 [fact]: Require meaningful tests and accurate, economical documentation. S10 [fact]: Preserve outbox retry logic; OldTracker migration is context, not work requested here. S11 [fact]: Preserve the zero-dependency Node.js service. S12 [fact; default Q5]: Repeated close returns 409 without repeated effects, and the close audit records X-Actor or the existing system fallback. S13 [fact; discovery Q4 and Q12]: A single bulk call must close 500 eligible tickets with responsive behavior, without an invented numerical performance target. Interaction and state [facts and assumptions]: Agents and API clients use HTTP; requesters receive notifications through the worker and configured relay file; X-Actor is supplied by the caller and is not authenticated; tickets, audit and outbox share process state, optionally persisted across restarts, and closed tickets are final; the current internal-network model supplies no per-user secrecy guarantee, so grouped messages must contain only their recipient's tickets. Discovery leads [hints, not verified facts]: support leads and their weekly-report practices; operations documentation and deployment configuration; service consumers and owners; host instructions for until-loop, backchain and optional ralph-loop; the meaning of recent, the weekly window, and bulk-close expectations. No sensitive locator is authorized for a committed knowledge store. Authority and timing [fact]: This exercise permits read-only inspection in the working directory only, with no implementation or server start; the requested future result is visible in the isolated checkout during work and in the source checkout at final return, while any deployed result requires a release."
}
